title: The Shivering Swimmer
briefing: Jonah, 12, jumped into the lake on the first warm day of spring. After ten minutes he climbs out shivering hard, his lips look a bit blue, and the hair on his arms is standing up. His friend says, “You're fine, it's sunny!”
question: Is Jonah's body doing something smart?

clues.title: Cold water, warm air
clues.text: The air is 75 °F but the lake is 58 °F. He felt fine on the dock and cold within a minute of getting in.
clues.shows: that the cold water, not the air, is pulling heat out of him

clues.title: Shivering
clues.text: His jaw and arms are shaking in fast little movements he can't stop, even when he tries.

clues.title: Pale skin, bluish lips
clues.text: His fingers are white and his lips blue-tinged — but his chest feels warm when he touches it.
clues.shows: blood moved away from the skin while the middle stays warm

clues.title: Towel and sun
clues.text: Wrapped in a towel in the sun, the shivering stops in about five minutes and his colour comes back.
clues.shows: everything reversing as soon as he warms up

hypotheses.text: Jonah is scared of the water.
hypotheses.flaw: Fear does not turn your fingers white or stop the instant you get a towel — and he was happy to jump in.

hypotheses.text: His body is losing heat to the cold water, so it makes heat (shivering) and keeps warm blood near his organs (pale skin).
He is allergic to lake water.
hypotheses.flaw: An allergy would cause itching or a rash, not shivering, and it would not vanish in five minutes of sunshine.

hypotheses.text: He swam so hard he is exhausted.
hypotheses.flaw: Hard swimming makes you hot and flushed, not pale and cold — and he was only in for ten minutes.

prediction.prompt: As the water gets colder — from a warm bath to a cold lake — what happens to how much Jonah shivers?

second.question: And blood flow to his skin?

concepts.label: cold takes heat
concepts.hint: What was the water doing to his body heat?

concepts.label: shivering makes heat
concepts.hint: What does all that shaking actually do?

concepts.label: blood away from skin
concepts.hint: Why did his fingers and lips change colour?

concepts.label: keeping the inside warm
concepts.hint: What is the body protecting by doing this?

concepts.label: stops when warm
concepts.hint: What happened once he was out and wrapped up?

transfer.context: Aiko waits at a windy winter bus stop without a coat. She notices she is shivering and her hands have gone white.
options: Her body is losing heat to the cold air, so her muscles shiver to make heat and blood stays near her organs.
She has a cold coming on.
transfer.retryHint: White hands and shivering, in the cold — which two of Jonah's clues does that match?
transfer.explanation: Cold air pulls heat from Aiko just as cold water did from Jonah. Her body responds the same two ways: shivering muscles make heat, and blood is kept away from the skin so the organs stay warm — which is why her hands look white.

takeaway: Your body guards its inside temperature. In the cold it makes heat with shivering and keeps warm blood away from the skin — looking pale is the body being smart, not sick.
